sources.text: Rockstar Games have released 38 new screenshots of Grand Theft Auto 6 , ahead of its release later this month. These screenshots, found on a dedicated launch gallery website Rockstar has created , prompts viewers to scroll down and take in the sights of several high quality in-game screenshots snapshotting all kinds of people, places, and events. These include, but are not limited to, a DJ set in-action, a man and his pitbull looking tough to the camera, a tattooed man getting his hair done (machine gun on hand), and a daring motorbike escape. However, my personal favourite has got to be a lively shot of a dive bar. A band - seemingly called The Rusty Anchor is playing - and some older ladies appear to be having a friendly chat with an open-shirt-wearing geezer enjoying a beer. You can find all the new images in an image gallery below. So look through them at your pleasure: Grand Theft Auto 6 is due to release on the 19th November on PS5, and Xbox Series X/S. A few days prior, Rockstar employees are voting on whether or not they'd like to officially recognise a developer union , as the Rockstar vs IWBG union employment tribunal comes to a close on the eve of GTA 6's release date.

sources.title: A bunch of Grand Theft Auto games will be cheap on Steam until GTA 6 comes out, and only one sucks
sources.text: In the run-up to GTA 6 's November 19 launch, Rockstar has multiple classic Grand Theft Auto games on sale on Steam – and, nearest I can tell, only on Steam. The Nintendo Switch eShop actually has a competing deal for the Grand Theft Auto Definitive Edition Trilogy, which is down 67% to $19.79, but that sale ends in 11 hours from the time of writing. On Steam, several GTA games are discounted until November 19 for an obviously timed special promotion. On Steam, you'll find four games on sale via two actual products: You can't argue with GTA 4 for $6, but you might argue with this version of, in particular, GTA 3. The Definitive Edition Trilogy was famously panned at launch for wonky graphics and poor technical performance that, for the most part, has been patched up in the years since. However, the PC port for GTA 3's Definitive Edition is uniquely poorly rated for reasons that will sound familiar. Here's how the three games in this trilogy compare in Steam reviews: The reception to the two other games in the trilogy improved over time while GTA 3 steadily declined. Much like the day-one reviews, today's Steam players complain of Rockstar launcher interference, bugs, shoddy art, broken cinematics, and performance dips. Weekly digests, tales from the communities you love, and more Curiously, perhaps unrelated to the quality of the port, some of today's gamers also don't seem to take too kindly to GTA 3's design sensibilities, it being slightly older than Vice City and San Andreas, and certainly a rawer open-world experience. Thomas Williamson, the CEO of the outsourced trilogy's original developer, Grove Street Games, said earlier this year that the criticism faced at launch was deserved. "I agreed with most of the people's reactions," he said. "But unfortunately, I feel like we did not agree with how the game was released and the response to it from a development side. And I think that would have changed the narrative significantly." However, he added, "at the end of the day, looking at the behind-the-scenes metrics on those games, there were a lot of people who were playing them and really enjoying them." You won't find Grove Street Games listed on the store pages for these games anymore. Previously, Williamson called it a "dick move" for Rockstar to have Grove Street's name removed. GTA 6 being pirated is just "a fact of life," says CEO of Rockstar owner, and lawyers are ready if it becomes a problem Austin has been a game journalist for 12 years, having freelanced for the likes of PC Gamer, Eurogamer, IGN, Sports Illustrated, and more while finishing his journalism degree. He's been with GamesRadar+ since 2019. They've yet to realize his position is a cover for his career-spanning Destiny column, and he's kept the ruse going with a lot of news and the occasional feature, all while playing as many roguelikes as possible. sources.title: Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble Shutting Down Less Than a Year After Launch
sources.text: It was announced less than a year ago, but Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble — a mobile spin-off of the flagship PlayStation series — has been canceled. Today marks the final update to the game, and it will shut down entirely in May 2027. The game was technically still in a soft launch phase, ahead of a full global release. "We’ve made the difficult decision to cease development of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble. The final planned update will be rolling out November 6th, 2026, and the app will be removed from stores on November 21st, 2026. Players who already have the game will be able to continue playing until May 1st, 2027, when the game’s servers will permanently shut down. On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development!" According to the official announcement, in-app purchases have been removed from the game, with the announcement advising players to use any in-game rewards or currency before the game shuts down. In an FAQ, players seeking some sort of refund for money spent are directed to Apple’s App Store or Google Play customer support. The game offered arena shooter-style action with characters from the series and was developed by Oh BiBi in collaboration with Insonmiac Games and PlayStation Studios. As recently as July, the PlayStation blog shared that the game was "gearing up for global launch" after "a successful testing phase shaped by player feedback." Rachel Weber is the Head of Editorial Development at IGN and an elder millennial. She's been a professional nerd since 2006 when she got her start on Official PlayStation Magazine in the UK, and has since worked for GamesIndustry.Biz, Rolling Stone and GamesRadar. She loves horror, horror movies, horror games, Red Dead Redemption 2, and her Love and Deepspace boyfriends.

sources.title: Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble canceled
sources.text: Free-to-play multiplayer arena shooter Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble has been canceled, publisher Sony Interactive Entertainment and developer Oh BiBi announced. The game soft-launched for iOS and Android in the Philippines and Indonesia alongside its announcement in November 2025, followed by Norway, Sweden, Finland, and Denmark in December 2025, Canada in May 2026, and the United Kingdom in August 2026. In a message posted to the game’s official website , Oh BiBi said a final update is being released today, and the game will be removed from storefronts on November 21. Servers will officially close on May 1, 2027. ■ Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble Update (November 6, 2026) We’ve made the difficult decision to cease development of Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble . The final planned update will be rolling out November 6, 2026, and the app will be removed from stores on November 21, 2026. Players who already have the game will be able to continue playing until May 1, 2027, when the game’s servers will permanently shut down. On behalf of the dev team and everyone helping to make the game, thanks to our amazing community for all your support, especially to those who have spent time playing, sharing feedback, and helping shape Ranger Rumble throughout its development! Game servers will permanently shut down on May 1, 2027. Can I continue playing after the game is removed from stores? If you already installed the game, you will be able to continue playing the game until End of Service on May 1, 2027. Will I still be able to download and reinstall the game? If you’re an existing player, Yes, until November 21, 2026, after that the game will be delisted from Apple’s App Store and Google Play. Will the game still work after the servers have been shut down? No, once the game servers are shutdown on May 1, 2027, the game will no longer load. Will there be any additional game updates? No, there are no planned updates after November 7, 2026. Will existing game modes, multiplayer matchmaking and competitive features remain available? All current game modes, matchmaking and competitive features will remain active until End of Service on May 1, 2027. Will there be any final events, rewards or opportunities to unlock content? The Qwark Pass seasons will continue to run until May 1, 2027, and the Super Pass is now free, and all content can be earned throughout each season. What happens to my Quark Pass and any unclaimed rewards? You have until End of Service on May 1, 2027, to enter, claim and utilize any rewards earned through play. No, in-app purchases have been removed. You can continue to earn rewards through play and spending that currency on upgrades, cosmetics, characters and currencies. What happens to my unused in-game currency? You have until End of Service on May 1, 2027, to use any currency you’ve earned or purchased. Can I request a refund for previous purchases? Your eligibility for a refund for any purchases made will be through Apple’s App Store or Google Play. What happens to my account and game progress after shut-down? All player data will be wiped from the servers at the End of Service, May 1, 2027. If you want to delete your data ahead of May 1, 2027, you can contact support here. Can I transfer my progress, purchases or unlocked items to another game? No, your progress and items are not transferable to any other game. What happens if I registered for the game or earned pre-registration rewards? Pre-registration rewards will be available to all players logging into the November 7, 2026 update. What happens to my personal data after the game closes? All player data will be deleted at End of Service, on May 1, 2027. Does this affect other Ratchet & Clank games or PlayStation services? No, Ratchet & Clank: Ranger Rumble ‘s ceasing development has no impact on other Ratchet & Clank games or PlayStation services.

sources.title: Skyrim Game Director Has a Very Specific Wishlist For The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel
sources.text: The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is probably still a couple years away , and we don't know much about Bethesda's next big RPG. However, the game director for Skyrim has come out with a couple of specific requests for the game. Former Bethesda design director Bruce Nesmith sat down on The Examined Game podcast to talk about his time at the company. But, about 40 minutes into the interview, the YouTuber asked Nesmith about what he'd like to see from The Elder Scrolls VI, and there are two things, better mounts and better ladders. And that latter one is how you can tell that he's a game director. Wanting better mounts in Elder Scrolls is almost universal for fans, as Skyrim doesn't exactly have a great mount system. As Nesmith describes the problem, "you can ride a horse, but that's all you can do in Skyrim. Thats it. You just ride the horse. Well, I should be able to do other things with the horse, too, like maybe fight on the horse, or have it fight with me, or you know, stuff like that." To be clear, Nesmith now spends his days writing novels, and doesn't have anything to do with Sentinel, but it would be cool to be able to have some kind of mounted combat system in The Elder Scrolls VI. For instance, I've been getting back into Monster Hunter Wilds ahead of the expansion, and the way you can use your Seikret to dodge out of boss mechanics and manage your inventory while avoiding attacks is huge, and would be great in other RPGs. But as for ladders, Nesmith request seems odd until he starts to explain the way that ladders limited game design in Skyrim. As he explains, "you don't climb up and down ladders. It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders, which really limits the art team in terms of how they can do multi-layer things. You know, all the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, and poof you're at the top. Or you have to climb a stair." Some of that is obviously the limited technology of 2011, but it's apparently something Bethesda tried to solve, before giving up to prioritize other elements of the massive RPG. When Nesmith tried to get ladders solved in Skyrim, he says "to do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions that our programmers very legitimately put in front of us and said, 'you give me answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's going to take to make them.' and that caused problems right there." Even when I sit down and think about it, I can't really think of any game that really nails ladders, and a lot of games have problems with them in one way or another, especially around the era of Skyrim. Nesmith goes on to explain a lot of the specific problems that enemy AI has with ladders, like its ability to decide whether or not to wait for you at the top, or to climb back down the ladder to come after you. These problems have all been solved in one way or another in other games, but I'd hope that Skyrim finds a way to solve the issue as well. Either way, The Elder Scrolls VI: Sentinel is still a few years away, even though Bethesda is already selling merch . We'll have to wait a bit to see more about the game, but there are some signs about what might be in the game, and that might even include ship combat – or at least I hope. Jackie Thomas is the Senior Tech Editor at IGN and the PC components queen. She's been covering gaming hardware for more than a decade for IGN, TechRadar, Gizmodo, PC Gamer and more. You can follow her @Jackiecobra

sources.name: PC Gamer
sources.title: Skyrim's lead designer has 2 big asks of The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel, and only one of them is something most players have ever thought about
sources.text: The classic children's board game: horses and ladders. Psst, hey kid, what are the big changes you'd like to see in The Elder Scrolls 6: Sentinel ? Because all have them, don't we? We've all got our big lists for Todd Howard: Five Easy Ways to Turn This Enormously Profitable Ship Around. You know who else has some changes he'd like to see in Sentinel? Bethesda alum and Skyrim lead designer Bruce Nesmith, who recently sat down with The Examined Game and said that the things he'd really like Bethesda to knuckle down on in TES 6 are mounts and ladders. "I'd like to see a much better implementation of mounts," said Nesmith. "That's been a common complaint; I'm not alone in that." But mounts can be hard to get right. "They're really tricky, there's a lot of hard decisions to be made in those. "You can ride a horse, but that's all you can do in Skyrim. That's it, you just ride the horse. Well, I should be able to do some other things too, maybe fight on the horse, or have it fight with me, you know, stuff like that." In fairness, Skyrim does have some fairly rudimentary mounted combat—though players had to wait for it to be added in a patch back in the day—but I suspect Nesmith would like to see something a bit less awkward in future Elder Scrolls games. I imagine a lot of players would echo Nesmith on mounts. I'm less sure they share his concern about ladders, which strikes me as a very charming and very game-designer-y fixation to have. "You don't climb up and down ladders [in current Elder Scrolls games]. It seems simple, it seems stupid, but you don't climb up and down ladders!" But you know what? I'm on board. Not having proper ladders, says Nesmith, "really limits the art team in terms of how they can do multi-layer things. You know, all the ladders in Skyrim, you click on the ladder, poof you're at the top, or you have to climb a stair." Advanced ladder tech has its costs, though. "To do ladders, you have to deal with a whole host of questions, which our programmers very legitimately put in front of us, and said 'You gimme answers to these, I'll tell you how much programming time it's gonna take to make them'. And that caused problems, right there". Keep up to date with the most important stories and the best deals, as picked by the PC Gamer team. There are, it turns out, a whole lot of ladder questions that arise if you try to implement them in your game. If two people use a ladder at once, what happens? How do NPCs make strategic decisions about them? How do you create animations and behaviours for characters getting hit while climbing, or dying while climbing? All these things and more pile up, which is why Bethesda decided to spend its time on other stuff, historically. Now, of course, it's not Nesmith's problem, and the man wants his mounts and ladders. Bravely, as someone else who also does not have to design The Elder Scrolls 6, I say give them to him. One of Josh's first memories is of playing Quake 2 on the family computer when he was much too young to be doing that, and he's been irreparably game-brained ever since. His writing has been featured in Vice, Fanbyte, and the Financial Times. He'll play pretty much anything, and has written far too much on everything from visual novels to Assassin's Creed. His most profound loves are for CRPGs, immersive sims, and any game whose ambition outstrips its budget. He thinks you're all far too mean about Deus Ex: Invisible War. sources.title: Nintendo says it isn't planning any more Switch 2 price hikes
sources.text: Nintendo, which unveiled the results of the first half of its fiscal year 2027 earlier today , has now said it has access to enough quantities of memory to manufacture more Switch 2 consoles. As a result, the platform holder does not plan to increase the price of the Switch 2. That's according to Reuters , citing Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa. Nintendo, which has so far sold 26m Switch 2 consoles, has already raised the price of the console earlier this year. The price hikes, which took effect on 1st September in the US, Canada, Japan and Europe, saw the console's price increase by $50 / €30 / ¥10,000. Although that was technically the first price hike for the console itself, prior to the Switch 2's launch last year, Nintendo raised the price of Switch 2 accessories in the US as a result of the Trump Administration's tariffs. The reason that would cause Nintendo to raise prices again is the same that already caused rival PlayStation and Xbox to do so: AI-driven, global memory and storage shortages . PlayStation already raised PS5 and PS5 Pro prices , on several occasions . Xbox has likewise gone through multiple rounds of price hikes for its Series X and Series S consoles , with the most recent having taken place in August . That same crisis pushed one of Nintendo's longtime ROM suppliers to exit the business , opting instead to focus on the more lucrative business segments. ROM memory is used in Switch cartridges, though Nintendo hasn't commented on the news. Incidentally, Switch 2 hardware sales have been in decline for several quarters now compared to its banner launch in 2025. Still, Switch 2 sales are tracking ahead of the Switch 1.

sources.title: Nintendo says it’s not planning another Switch 2 price hike
sources.text: Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo’s president says it will have ‘sufficient’ RAM as shortages drive up console prices.﻿ Nintendo president Shuntaro Furukawa said during the company’s latest earnings call that it’s “not considering additional changes” to the Switch 2’s price, Reuters reports. The Switch 2 got a $50 price hike earlier this year, bringing its starting price up to $499. Nintendo said in Thursday’s earnings report that Switch 2 sales have dropped 37.4 percent year-over-year. According to Reuters , Furukawa also gave an update on the RAM shortage, saying, “There has been no major change to the memory situation and Nintendo is in a position to secure sufficient quantities.” Earlier this week, one of Nintendo’s Switch 2 cartridge suppliers announced it plans to stop making ROM memory to focus on memory for data centers instead. Demand from AI data centers is driving the ongoing RAM shortages that’s leading to a wave of tech price increases. Microsoft has raised Xbox Series X / S prices multiple times now, increasing the Series S’s starting price from $299 to $499. The PS5 has also been hit with price hikes, taking its starting price up to $649 .

sources.title: What to do in Goron City in the Ocarina of Time Remake
sources.text: Goron City and Darunia in the OOT Remake have players try to cheer up the gloomy Goron Goron City in Zelda Ocarina of Time Remake is a fiery mountain home, run by the equally fiery Darunia, who is miserable for a number of reasons and will need cheering up if you want his assistance. To do so will require a bit of a runaround, taking you all the way to the Lost Woods and back again, but it's worth it (and also mandatory if you want to progress the plot of the Switch 2 Remake). If you're having trouble working out what to do next, I'll explain how to solve the mystery of Goron City in a full walkthrough and guide, taking you through all the steps needed in this section of The Legend of Zelda Ocarina of Time. If you're approaching Goron City, you'll need to be prepared against fire. Find out how to get a metal, non-flammable shield in our guide on how to get a Shield and Sword in Zelda Ocarina of Time . When you first reach Goron City in the Ocarina of Time Remake, you'll discover that all the Gorons are miserable and that their leader, Darunia, has holed himself up in his room. The main goal here is to access Darunia and cheer him up . Here's how you do that: With Darunia placated, he'll be willing to give you Spiritual Stone of Fire... Except he doesn't have it. You'll have to go to the Dodongo Cavern and find it there. Fortunately, he will give you Goron Bracelet, which will allow you to pick up Bomb Flowers and throw them! Feel like some side quests? sources.title: O que comprar na Black Friday 2026: TVs para games
sources.text: A Black Friday é uma das melhores oportunidades do ano para renovar a sala de entretenimento e investir em uma smart TV preparada para videogames . Com a evolução dos consoles e dos PCs gamers, escolher uma televisão deixou de ser apenas uma questão de tamanho de tela e recursos como baixa latência, fluidez de imagem e tecnologias de sincronização fazem toda a diferença durante as partidas. Mas, diante de tantas opções, como encontrar uma TV na Black Friday que realmente ofereça bom desempenho? Para ajudar na escolha, o TecMundo reuniu os principais critérios para avaliar uma TV gamer e cinco modelos de destaque de marcas renomadas. Uma boa TV gamer precisa combinar conectividade moderna, alta taxa de atualização, baixo input lag e qualidade de imagem. Também vale observar o tamanho da tela, o sistema de áudio e os recursos inteligentes, especialmente para quem pretende aproveitar jogos na nuvem e transformar a televisão no centro do entretenimento do lar. Leia também Smart TV 32 polegadas: as melhores opções de custo-benefício Smart TV 32 polegadas: as melhores opções de custo-benefício A presença de HDMI 2.1 é fundamental para aproveitar recursos como resolução 4K a 120 Hz, VRR e ALLM nos consoles compatíveis. Antes de investir no televisor novo, confira também quantas entradas oferecem esses recursos, principalmente se pretende conectar videogame, PC e soundbar simultaneamente, por exemplo. A taxa de atualização indica quantas vezes por segundo a tela atualiza a imagem. Para jogos, o ideal é procurar modelos com pelo menos 120 Hz nativos. Algumas TVs chegam a 144 Hz ou mais, oferecendo vantagens principalmente para quem utiliza computadores com placas de vídeo potentes ou costuma jogar games competitivos nos consoles. O input lag representa o atraso entre o comando enviado pelo controle e sua reprodução na tela , enquanto o tempo de resposta mede a velocidade com que os pixels mudam de estado na tela. Para quem procura uma TV gamer com o menor input lag para jogos competitivos , esses dois indicadores merecem atenção especial. Nestes casos, painéis OLED costumam se destacar pela resposta extremamente rápida, com modelos que alcançam menos de 1 ms. Leia também Smart TV OLED Samsung: dicas para escolher a ideal para você Smart TV OLED Samsung: dicas para escolher a ideal para você Muitas TVs modernas contam com tecnologias que aprimoram bastante a experiência de games. Recursos como AMD FreeSync Premium e NVIDIA G-Sync sincronizam a frequência da TV com os quadros gerados pela placa de vídeo, reduzindo cortes e travamentos. Já o VRR, sigla para Variable Refresh Rate , também contribui para uma experiência mais fluida, especialmente em jogos com oscilações na taxa de quadros. A tecnologia da tela influencia diretamente o contraste, o brilho e a reprodução de cores, e modelos atuais contam com diferentes tipos de painéis. O painel OLED , por exemplo, oferece pretos profundos e excelente tempo de resposta. Já Neo QLED, QLED e Mini LED são alternativas interessantes para quem prioriza brilho elevado. Na dúvida entre TV LED e Mini LED para jogar, vale apontar que a segunda leva vantagem no controle da iluminação e no contraste, especialmente em conteúdos HDR. Cupons de Black Friday Confira aqui os cupons de Black Friday que já estão disponíveis para resgate Confira aqui os cupons de Black Friday que já estão disponíveis para resgate A Black Friday é uma boa oportunidade para encontrar televisores premium com descontos e condições especiais. Pensando nisso, o TecMundo selecionou cinco sugestões de TV gamer para comprar na Black Friday , levando em consideração aspectos como desempenho, tecnologias de imagem e recursos para diferentes perfis de jogadores. A LG OLED evo C6 é uma das opções mais completas para quem procura desempenho de alto nível. Lançada em 2026, ela varia entre 42 e 83 polegadas e combina painel OLED 4K, frequência nativa de 120 Hz e VRR de até 165 Hz, além de compatibilidade com NVIDIA G-Sync e AMD FreeSync Premium. Seu tempo de resposta baixíssimo de 0,1 ms favorece imensamente todo tipo de partida, especialmente em jogos competitivos. O modelo também conta com HDMI 2.1, ALLM, Dolby Vision Gaming em 4K a 120 Hz e Painel de Jogos, que facilita o acesso às configurações durante as partidas. Seu principal diferencial é unir contraste e velocidade de resposta excepcionais, sendo indicada para jogadores competitivos, usuários de PC gamer e quem busca uma experiência premium também para filmes e séries. Fazendo parte da geração 2025, a Samsung OLED S90F combina painel OLED 4K com taxa de atualização de até 144 Hz, quatro entradas HDMI 2.1, VRR, AMD FreeSync Premium Pro e NVIDIA G-Sync, opções essenciais para quem costuma jogar na TV da sala. Entre seus principais destaques podemos citar HDR10+ Gaming, Game Bar e ALLM, além do Samsung Gaming Hub que permite acessar serviços como Xbox Cloud Gaming e NVIDIA GeForce NOW diretamente pela televisão. Para jogar pela nuvem, porém, é preciso ter uma assinatura ativa em um dos serviços disponíveis, bem como um controle compatível. Disponível em versões de 55, 65 e 77 polegadas, ela é uma escolha interessante para quem deseja jogar sem depender exclusivamente de um console conectado à TV, além de também ter tudo para agradar a quem procura excelente contraste e qualidade de imagem OLED. A TCL C7K é uma alternativa interessante para quem prefere uma televisão com brilho elevado, já que seu painel QD-Mini LED combina Quantum Dot e iluminação Mini LED, sendo capaz de oferecer controle preciso de luz, contraste e cores intensas. O modelo apresenta resolução 4K, 144 Hz VRR, HDMI 2.1 e AMD FreeSync Premium Pro, bem como recursos como Game Master, Game Bar e Superwide Gameview, este último oferecendo formatos de visualização ultrawide de 21:9 e 32:9. A linha abrange versões de 65, 75 e 115 polegadas, tendo como seu principal diferencial a combinação de desempenho gamer e brilho elevado, sendo especialmente indicada para salas iluminadas e jogadore

stories.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais
stories.summary: The post Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais appeared first on Xbox Wire em Português .

sources.name: Xbox Wire BR
sources.title: Assassin’s Creed Valhalla: a atualização com novo jogo+, novo recurso e muito mais
sources.text: A atualização mais pedida de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla já está disponível no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One. A atualização traz diversas novidades empolgantes ao jogo, oferecendo novas maneiras de aproveitar sua aventura viking. O grande destaque é a chegada do Novo Jogo+, um dos recursos mais pedidos pelos fãs de Assassin’s Creed Valhalla . As demais novidades do patch garantem que sua experiência após o fim da campanha e no Novo Jogo+ seja renovada e desafiadora, com recompensas que fazem tudo valer a pena. Confira o que esperar da atualização mais pedida: Conversamos com o designer-chefe de jogo, David Larouche, para saber mais sobre a atualização e como a equipe coloca os jogadores no centro de tudo o que faz. Quais novidades desta atualização são uma resposta direta aos comentários da comunidade? David Larouche : o Novo Jogo+ foi, sem dúvida, o recurso mais pedido pelos fãs. Assassin’s Creed Valhalla é um jogo imenso, mas, para algumas pessoas, jogar uma vez só não basta. Com esta atualização, estamos muito empolgados em permitir que nossos vikings mais dedicados vivam essa aventura novamente, mas, desta vez, com o personagem que tinham ao final da campanha. Como a equipe garantiu que os recursos pedidos atendessem às expectativas dos jogadores? DL : queríamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ não fosse apenas jogar tudo de novo; queríamos permitir que os jogadores continuassem aumentando seu poder, percebessem uma progressão em etapas menores e seguissem aprimorando seus personagens. Por todos esses motivos, adicionamos um modo de progressão estendida, mais melhorias para todas as peças de equipamento divino, uma nova categoria de runas e mais de 300 novas opções de bônus de runas que podem ser gravados na Forja de Runas — e todos esses recursos também estão disponíveis fora do Novo Jogo+. Com todas essas novidades, acreditamos que a experiência do Novo Jogo+ incentivará os jogadores a explorar todo o potencial de Eivor. Houve algum desafio inesperado na implementação dessas novidades? DL : acho que o mais surpreendente para nós foi justamente não termos encontrado nenhum grande desafio que nos deixasse sem saber como avançar. Conseguimos reunir uma equipe muito competente de desenvolvedores com experiência em adicionar o Novo Jogo+ a jogos já existentes; o processo de produção foi incrivelmente tranquilo. Há algum recurso que você esteja especialmente empolgado para ver no jogo? DL : com a atualização, transformamos praticamente todos os bônus presentes em itens em runas que podem ser gravadas na Forja de Runas, independentemente de terem sido lançados na experiência estendida, em uma expansão ou até mesmo na Loja. Mal posso esperar para ver como os jogadores vão combinar todos esses bônus e criar os mais variados tipos de sinergia. Tenho certeza de que há muitas combinações poderosíssimas a serem descobertas! Assassin’s Creed Valhalla recebeu sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos. Por que lançar a atualização mais pedida para os jogadores agora? DL : Valhalla pode ter recebido sua última atualização de conteúdo há anos, mas isso não significa que os jogadores deixaram de se importar com o jogo — e nós também não. Sabemos que o Novo Jogo+ é algo que a comunidade deseja há muito tempo e, quando surgiu a oportunidade de finalmente torná-lo realidade, mal podíamos esperar para seguir em frente. No fim das contas, trata-se de dar aos jogadores de longa data mais um motivo para voltar a um mundo ao qual dedicaram tanto tempo e reviver a jornada de Eivor sob uma nova perspectiva, levando consigo boa parte do que conquistaram pelo caminho. O fato de algum tempo ter passado não torna essa experiência menos significativa para nós nem, esperamos, para nossos jogadores. Qual é a importância da comunidade de Assassin’s Creed para a equipe da franquia? DL : a comunidade é extremamente importante para mim e para a equipe. Pessoalmente, acompanho as redes sociais com frequência para ver sobre o que os jogadores estão conversando e, como equipe, prestamos muita atenção aos comentários e às conversas pela internet. Adoramos ver o que os jogadores criam e compartilham sobre nossos jogos. Essa conexão com a comunidade é incrivelmente gratificante e é uma das principais razões pelas quais fazemos o que fazemos. Jogue hoje mesmo Assassin’s Creed Valhalla com a atualização mais pedida no XBOX Series X|S e no XBOX One.

sources.name: Eurogamer
sources.title: PlayStation sees record high player numbers and increased revenue for Q2 2026, and a lot of that success is down to Marvel's Wolverine
sources.text: As part of today's (Thursday 5th November, 2026) financial results, Sony has confirmed that monthly active users, referred to as MAU, across both PlayStation 4 and 5, reached 127 million in September. This represents a seven percent growth year-on-year for the company, and sets a new record high. In Layman's terms, this simply means that more people are engaged with the PlayStation ecosystem now than ever before. And it's not just that there are more people using machines and occasionally booting up their consoles; active play time also increased over the past quarter, too, with total logged play time increasing by four percent, year-on-year. As a result, Sony and PlayStation noted that its Game & Network Services division saw revenue grow by nine percent year-on-year, resulting in operating profit rising by 83 percent year-on-year. Notably, despite its mixed reception , Marvel's Wolverine was name-checked as a driving force for the decent performance over the past quarter - but that shouldn't be a surprise for anyone that's actually been paying attention to how the game performed . The game sold through 2.4 million copies as of 4th November (so, in roughly 50 days). Ghost of Yotei , meanwhile, has sold through 3.3 million since its launch in October 2025. More people playing consoles, and for longer - it must all be good news for Sony right? Well, not all the graphs are showing growth. PS5 hardware sales continue to gradually decline: in the reporting period, Sony sold 2.6 million PS5 consoles, down from 4 million in the same quarter in 2025. But, with 100 million PS5 units out in the wild, and 127 million PlayStation accounts across the whole ecosystem, Sony doesn't seem that worried: instead, the company is now focusing on converting those with active accounts into more viable customers. Elsewhere in the results, we heard from Sony CFO Lin Tao that the PlayStation 6 is on track and "progressing as scheduled" , with "solid progress" expected on the machine in 2027. Regarding those falling PS5 sales, Tao also referenced that, and says it's all part of the natural cycle of console launches and iteration. "Although new PS5 unit sales are gradually declining as expected at this stage of the console life cycle, the PlayStation platform continues to expand and grow in a stable manner," Tao explained. "[Next year,] we intend to make solid progress in preparing for the next-generation platform." It must be encouraging for Sony to see this growth in this quarter, especially after all the bad press and furore around the company's decision to end the manufacturing of PlayStation discs by January 2028 . It seems to be a core part of the gaming audience's understanding of game ownership, the decision has been widely contested as anti-consumer. It's caused a lot of bad blood with PlayStation players over the past six months, but - seemingly, given these results - that has translated to very little material impact on Sony's bottom line.
